pillar_reactions.evidence: Not delivered as the standard pillar pitch — it arrived as a screen-share of the $200/month membership contents: 'full tutorials of every movement you would ever do with the kettlebell single double all the combinations everything', three staged three-month plans, and 'You then have all of our mobility stuff. That'll be important for you for the pain.' The prospect's entire response was 'Okay... I'll check it out.'

Never presented. The nutrition philosophy was not delivered at all; food appeared only as one word inside the membership feature list ('it's got food') after the prospect had said 'food I'm pretty good with' and the rep let it go.

Reduced to a group feature — 'once a week, you have a live call with Trevor on Thursdays, which is a group class. You can do Q&A' — despite the rep having correctly identified accountability as the need minutes earlier: 'Accountability, also just making, sounds like you want to plan something that's different.' The prospect asked nothing and agreed.

anchors.raw: I know how to train, it's not like I need a trainer, I know how to train, but maybe sometimes you like, don't push enough or you don't go, you know, the extra mile
anchors.note: The anchor is his own free four-year practice, which he rates as adequate on knowledge and deficient only on intensity. Against that, coaching has to be worth $1,000 a month for motivation alone. Nobody attacked the premise — that a self-programmed trainee who is training twice a week on four hours of sleep does not in fact know how to solve this.

anchors.raw: we have something that's it's $200 a month and essentially it's pretty much everything you could ever need
anchors.note: The strongest price-undercutting anchor on this call was introduced by the rep, not the prospect, and described as 'pretty much everything you could ever need' and 'probably all you need'. Any prospect who hears that framing has been given a reason never to pay $6,000.

unmet_demand.want: Someone to push him harder in the moment than he pushes himself
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep asked the clarifying question — 'so you're looking for someone to like push you whilst you are training? Like, in the moment?' — and then never answered it. Neither the coaching nor the membership provides live in-session pushing; the membership answer is a weekly group Q&A.

unmet_demand.want: New inputs and a different approach after four years of the same self-directed routine
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Almost certainly served by tailored one-to-one programming, but the tailored programme was never described. He was shown a library of pre-recorded plans, which is the same category of thing he already has.

unmet_demand.want: To know what was actually being offered — he asked directly
unmet_demand.why_unmet: 'What exactly is the thing you're offering to understand?' was answered with 'Everything is completely tailored' and then a pivot to a $200/month membership. He left the call without ever being told the one-to-one coaching product exists.

unmet_demand.want: Relief from shoulder, back, elbow and knee pain
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Addressed with one line pointing at a self-serve mobility library ('That'll be important for you for the pain'). No assessment, no screening and no supervision behind it.
